summary: Working in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies, the 13th Dalai Lama studied under Agvan Dorzhiev (~1898–1910), Tertön Sogyal (~1895–1904), Pa Ri Rabsal, Lobsang Lungtok Tenzin Thinley, Gendun Tendzin Gyatso, Jampa Gyatso, Ngawang Pelden Chokyi Gyeltsen, and Yeshe Chopel.

Active in Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Tibetology, the 14th Dalai Lama studied under teachers including Tsenshab Serkong Rinpoche (1948–1983), Trijang Lobsang Yeshe Tenzin Gyatso (1951), and Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen (~1968–1977). He founded the Mind and Life Institute in 1990.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje studied under meditation teacher Kalu Rinpoche, Beru Khyentse Rinpoche I, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche.
Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, the 19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche studied under Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen (~1930–1940), Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, and Khangsar Dorje Chang.

id: P:3rd Sras Rinpoche Thubten Kalsang Bstanpai Gyaltsen
summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he studied under the 96th Ganden Tripa Thubten Kunga, at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1950–1971), and Gyume Tantric College (1971). He later held posts at Drepung Loseling Monastery (1984) and Gyume Tantric College (1995–2008).

Active in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Drepung Monastery (~1951–1959). He served at Central School for Tibetans, Shimla (1960), Central School for Tibetans (1965–1970), and was principal of the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (1971–2001).
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Shenphen Nangwa and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso.
Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, A Dzom Gyalsé Gyurmé Dorjé studied under Khenpo Ngawang Pelzang and Ayu Khandro.
He studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1908–1911). He subsequently held posts at Pachaiyappa's College (1911–1918) and served as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).
An Indologist, A. B. Gajendragadkar served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College.
Active in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies, McDermott studied under W. Norman Brown. She held a post attested in 1969 at the University of Wisconsin–Milwaukee.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology, Muller completed his PhD at Stony Brook University under Sung-Bae Park. He held academic posts at Toyo Gakuen University (1994–2008), the University of Tokyo (2005; 2008–2019), and Musashino University (2019).
Specializing in Indology and linguistics, A. Fürst studied at the University of Tübingen under Richard von Garbe.
Active in Indology and religious studies, A. G. Mohan studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya (~1971–1989) and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

A philosopher, Armstrong graduated from Jesus College, Cambridge (BA, 1932). He held posts at Swansea University (1936–1939), the University of Malta (1939), Cardiff University (1946), and was Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).

Active in history, archaeology, and philosophy, Sabra studied at Alexandria University, the University of London, and the London School of Economics under Karl Popper (~1950–1955). He held posts at the Warburg Institute (1962–1972) and Harvard University (1972–1996).

Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Ramanujan earned degrees from Maharaja's College, Mysore, and Indiana University Bloomington. He served at the University of Chicago from 1962, becoming full professor in 1968 and William E. Colvin Professor in 1983.

Active in Indology and philosophy, A. Mahadeva Sastri served as curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and later as director of the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

An Indologist, Aiyangar studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar. He served as joint editor at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and Brahmavidyā (attested 1942), and as librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

Working in linguistics and Indology, Narasimhia earned a PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933). He held posts at the University of Mysore and Maharaja's College, Mysore, serving as librarian and part-time professor of philology.
